scores.claim_text: Space and Defense segment includes space-launch-vehicle, satellite and spacecraft components; FY 2024 gross-margin improvement attributed to space vehicle development programs.
supports: pentagon_jbook: National Security Space Launch Program (PE 1206853SF) FUNDED_SHRINKING — FY24 $157M, FY25 $103M, FY26 $6.6M (96% cut vs FY24)
pentagon_jbook: Evolved Strategic SATCOM (PE 1206855SF) FUNDED_GROWING — FY24 $474M → FY26 $1,230M
Mixed signal: launch RDT&E (NSSL) is being wound down to near-zero (FUNDED_SHRINKING) while satellite SATCOM RDT&E (ESS) is funded growing
scores.interpretation: Mixed J-Book signal for Moog's space program exposure. The launch-vehicle RDT&E line that supports launcher thrust-vector controls (NSSL) is being wound down to $6.6M in FY26 — consistent with development-phase work ending and procurement shifting elsewhere. The SATCOM line is healthy. Because Moog cites both launchers and satellites without ranking either as material individually, treat as MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY: a portion of Space segment R&D-funded exposure is shrinking, but the overall segment narrative is not contradicted (production/procurement of launch vehicles continues outside the RDT&E line).

summary.overall_assessment: No J-Book divergence pattern detected at the cutoff date. Moog's named high-priority programs (F-35, AEGIS BMD, JATM, ESS) are FUNDED_STEADY or FUNDED_GROWING in the FY 2026 J-Book. One mixed signal (Space launch RDT&E shrinking) is balanced by SATCOM growth in the same segment. USAspending confirms $221M of direct DoD revenue (2022-2026). Backlog narrative is supported by the forward funding picture. MOG-A does not exhibit the canonical YSS/IONQ-style 'company depends on a program the Pentagon has zeroed out' pattern.
